## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on the integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\), the literal all-degree certificate is established: for every \(0\le k\le i+j+1\), the admissible \(P_{x,k-x}\), including the terminal class, and all one- and two-term Pieri rows are classified below, and their lattice equals \((A_+M)_{d+k}\).

## Strategy
Let \(i,j\ge1\), \(d=ij\), \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\), and assume
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+k}}\mathbb Zs_\mu ,
\qquad M_{d+k}=0\ (k<0\text{ or }k>i+j+1).
\]
For \(0\le x\le j,\ 0\le y\le i\), set
\[
P_{x,y}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},y)}
\]
(with \(y=0\) omitted), and set
\[
P_{j+1,0}:=s_{(i+1)^{j+1}}.
\]

For \(0\le k\le i+j\), put
\[
\alpha_k=\max(0,k-i),\qquad \beta_k=\min(j,k),\qquad C_x=P_{x,k-x}.
\]
Then
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=\alpha_k}^{\beta_k}\mathbb ZC_x.
\]
Indeed, a partition in the interval has \(x\) rows of length \(i+1\), \(j-x\) rectangle rows of length \(i\), and one final row of length \(y\le i\), so \(x+y=k\). At the final degree,
\[
M_{d+i-j?}=0
\]
is not intended; rather, at \(K=i+j+1\),
\[
M_{d+K}=\mathbb ZP_{j+1,0}.
\]

For \(1\le k\le i+j\), the complete \(h_1\)-row set is indexed by
\(x\in[\alpha_{k-1},\beta_{k-1}]\):
\[
R_x=h_1P_{x,k-1-x}
=[x\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]]C_x+
[x+1\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]]C_{x+1}. \tag{1}
\]
Thus the boundary one-term rows are explicitly:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{source}&\text{row}\\ \hline
k\ge i+1&P_{\alpha_k-1,k-1-(\alpha_k-1)}&C_{\alpha_k}\\
k\ge j+1&P_{j,k-1-j}&C_j .
\end{array}
\]
In the first row, the absent putative term is
\(P_{\alpha_k-1,i+1}\), which is outside the indexing range \(y\le i\).
In the second, the absent putative term is
\(P_{j+1,k-j-1}\), which is undefined unless \(k=i+j+1\).

At \(k=i+j+1\), the sole \(h_1\)-row is
\[
h_1P_{j,i}=P_{j+1,0}. \tag{2}
\]

Now let \(1\le t\le k\). Since \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\),
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=\sum_{t=1}^{k}h_tM_{d+k-t}. \tag{3}
\]
For a source \(P_{u,k-t-u}\), Pieri gives, after restriction to the interval,
\[
h_tP_{u,k-t-u}
=[u\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]]C_u+
[u+1\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]]C_{u+1}. \tag{4}
\]
The two possibilities are respectively: add all \(t\) boxes to the final row; or add one box in column \(i+1\) and the remaining \(t-1\) boxes to the final row. No other horizontal strip remains in the interval, since two enlarged \(i\)-rows would repeat column \(i+1\).

If a term on the right side of (4) exists, then \(u\in[\alpha_{k-1},\beta_{k-1}]\), and (4) is exactly the \(h_1\)-row \(R_u\) from (1); if neither term exists, it is zero. At the terminal degree, every nonzero \(h_t\)-row is the row \(P_{j+1,0}\) in (2). Hence
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}
=
L_k:=
\sum_{x=\alpha_{k-1}}^{\beta_{k-1}}\mathbb ZR_x
\quad(1\le k\le i+j),
\]
and
\[
(A_+M)_{d+i+j+1}=\mathbb ZP_{j+1,0},\qquad
(A_+M)_d=0. \tag{5}
\]

For checkable unit data, let \(b=\min(i,j)\). If \(1\le k\le b\), then
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}),
\]
and deleting \(C_0\) gives a lower unitriangular \(k\times k\) matrix, of determinant \(1\). If \(b<k\le i+j\), one boundary row is present. If \(i\le j\), the rows
\[
C_{\alpha_k},\ C_{\alpha_k}+C_{\alpha_k+1},\ldots,
C_{\beta_k-1}+C_{\beta_k}
\]
form a lower unitriangular square minor of determinant \(1\). If \(j<i\), the rows
\[
C_{\alpha_k}+C_{\alpha_k+1},\ldots,
C_{\beta_k-1}+C_{\beta_k},\ C_{\beta_k}
\]
form an upper unitriangular square minor of determinant \(1\). Thus \(L_k=M_{d+k}\) for \(k>b\), while (5) is the complete relation-lattice equality in every degree.

## Gaps
The proof uses the stipulated all-degree integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation. It does not independently source-ground or prove that presentation.

## Next
This certificate alone is established conditionally; no parent-theorem conclusion is made.
